summary:
Ulsan stands under the national framework of South Korea. No ordinance, municipal directive, police practice, court decision or documented incident specific to transgender people in Ulsan appeared in the available sources.

Two decisions are final and apply in Ulsan. An appellate court finalised an award of 300,000 won against the state, on a claim of 3 million won, over police advice given to a woman who had obtained court approval for a family-register gender change in 2020 telling her to avoid women's public restrooms; the court held that comfortable restroom use is a fundamental and universal human right. The advice the court condemned is a general police practice rather than an incident confined to one city, so the ruling reaches officers in Ulsan, though no comparable Ulsan complaint has been documented.

In May 2024 a regional court approved a registered-sex change from male to female for five transgender applicants who had not undergone sex-reassignment surgery. It held that gender change cannot be determined by surgery, that court guidelines requiring surgery are reference material rather than criteria, and that every person has the right to live according to their gender identity. Applications in Ulsan proceed on that footing; the sources record no Ulsan applicant and no Ulsan court ruling on the question.
tangentialFactors:
The rulings that shape a trans visitor's position in Ulsan were issued in other parts of the country. Their reach in Ulsan rests on general applicability rather than on any local instrument, and no Ulsan court has ruled on restroom access or on a registered-sex application.

The damages award is symbolic: 300,000 won against a claim of 3 million won. Its effect is declaratory, so deterrence of the restroom advice depends on officers and venue staff knowing the decision rather than on the size of the penalty.

No district-level or city-level breakdown of national survey evidence on restroom avoidance was identified, so the frequency of that problem in Ulsan cannot be stated.
localsOnly:
No Ulsan municipal ordinance, city office policy or transgender-specific service appeared in the sources. Residents depend on the national framework for registration, restroom access and remedies against officials or businesses.

A Ulsan resident applying to change registered sex does so through the courts on the footing set in May 2024, when a regional court held that surgery cannot determine gender change and that guidelines requiring it are reference only; five applicants who had not undergone surgery were approved.

Where police or a business tell a resident to avoid the restroom matching their gender, that advice has been held to infringe personal rights, with compensation of 300,000 won in the case that was finalised. The remedy is real but small, and no Ulsan resident has been documented bringing such a claim.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Ulsan has any municipal provision addressing discrimination on grounds of gender identity, and whether its police force has issued internal guidance on restroom advice or on the treatment of transgender detainees, is not sourced.

National survey figures on restroom avoidance are not broken down by city, and no Ulsan rate can be derived from them.

No Ulsan-specific incident, complaint or damages claim concerning a transgender person was located in the sources reviewed. The absence of a documented case is not evidence that none has occurred.
